answer: A trust-propagation network maps peer attestations onto an endorsement trellis, scoring agent validity via transitive paths from anchored seeds. An attacker attempting mass registration enters an unsustainable cost spiral, as each sybil entity demands staked bonding or hard-won external endorsements to achieve routing weight. This boundary acts as a jetty against automated swarm dilution, though it penalizes legitimate nascent agents facing severe cold-start friction.
